mcat_description.short: A frisking booth is a portable, prefabricated privacy enclosure used at security checkpoints to conduct pat-down body searches, primarily designed for female screening by female security personnel. Sold per unit, typically constructed with a mild steel or ACP-panel frame and privacy curtains or rigid walls.
mcat_description.long: Frisking booths are compact, portable security enclosures deployed at high-traffic entry points — airports, metro stations, shopping malls, corporate offices, stadiums, and government buildings — to provide a private, dignified space for security personnel to conduct manual body searches. The dominant Indian commercial form is the ladies frisking booth: a steel-framed or ACP-panel cabin approximately 4ft × 4ft × 6.5ft, with two rigid side panels and two open sides fitted with privacy curtains, mounted on wheels for easy repositioning. Construction materials include mild steel (powder-coated), ACP (aluminium composite panel), FRP (fibre-reinforced plastic), and PVC panels, with frame gauges typically 16-gauge MS pipe. Male variants exist as open-frame frisking stands or podiums without full enclosure, while premium variants include a roof, sliding door, and modular bolt-together assembly for permanent installations.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, 'frisking booth' refers almost exclusively to a portable privacy enclosure for manual security pat-down screening, with the ladies/female variant being the dominant commercial form driven by cultural norms requiring gender-segregated screening at public venues. The product is distinct from a security guard cabin (which houses a guard for access control) and from a walk-through metal detector gate (an electronic screening device). Key material variants are mild steel with powder coating, ACP (aluminium composite panel) with MS framework, and FRP (fibre-reinforced plastic) — with ACP-panel MS-frame booths being the most widely manufactured and quoted variant across Indian suppliers. Standard dimensions cluster around 4ft × 4ft × 6.5ft (approx. 1200 × 1200 × 2000 mm), with 2 rigid side panels and 2 open sides fitted with privacy curtains; wheeled bases for mobility are a near-universal feature. Premium variants include a full roof, sliding door, and modular bolt-together construction for permanent airport or metro installations. Male frisking stands/podiums are open-frame structures without enclosure, used at lower-security checkpoints. Buyers are predominantly institutional: airport operators, metro rail corporations, mall developers, corporate facility managers, and private security agencies. The product sits within the broader prefabricated portable cabin taxonomy but is a specialised security-use sub-category. No mandatory BIS or IS standard governs frisking booths specifically; buyers specify material grade, dimensions, and finish as custom requirements.
